lesson.text: Quick memory: what is an ostinato? (A pattern that repeats over and over.) Today: how songs are built from parts that come back.
Songs have parts, called sections. We give each new section a letter: the first is A. If it comes back, it is A again; a new one is B, then C.
Binary form is A B: two different parts. Ternary form is A B A: a part, a new part, then the first part again, like a sandwich. Listen: A, B, A.
In rondo form, the A section keeps coming back between new parts: A B A C A. Beethoven's Für Elise is a rondo.
Pop songs have verses and a chorus. Each verse has the same tune but new words; the chorus has the same tune and the same words every time, and it is usually the catchiest part.
A bridge is a new part, usually heard once near the end, so the last chorus feels fresh. An intro starts the song, and an outro ends it.
Worked example: verse, chorus, verse, chorus, bridge, chorus. The chorus comes 3 times, the verse twice and the bridge once.
Try it in the world: listen to a favourite song and write down its sections in order: intro, verse, chorus … How many times does the chorus come? Next: writing your own song.

exercises.prompt: What is the form A B A called?
exercises.hint: How many parts, and does the first come back?
exercises.explain: A, B, then A again: three parts, so ternary form.

exercises.prompt: A chorus has the same words and the same tune every time it comes.
exercises.hint: Think of the part everyone sings along to.
exercises.explain: True: the chorus repeats its words and its tune.

exercises.prompt: Match each section to what it is.
matches: a new part near the end
exercises.hint: Which part changes its words each time?
exercises.explain: Verses change their words, the chorus repeats everything, the bridge is new near the end, and the intro starts.

exercises.prompt: Listen to the two phrases. Is the second the same as the first, or new?
exercises.hint: Listen to the first phrase, then compare the second with it.
exercises.explain: Both phrases go C, E, G, E: the same, so it is A A.

exercises.prompt: How many times is the chorus played in this song?
exercises.hint: Touch each chorus block as you count.
exercises.explain: verse, chorus, verse, chorus, bridge, chorus: the chorus comes 3 times.

exercises.prompt: Listen to the three phrases (four notes each). Which form did you hear?
exercises.hint: Call the first phrase A. Is each next phrase the same (A again) or new (B)?
exercises.explain: The first phrase came back at the end: A B A.

exercises.prompt: In rondo form, which section keeps coming back?
exercises.hint: Look at A B A C A.
exercises.explain: The A section comes back between the new parts: A B A C A.

exercises.prompt: Put these sections in a typical song's order.
exercises.hint: The intro starts it; the bridge comes near the end.
exercises.explain: Intro, verse, chorus, then the bridge near the end, and a last chorus.

exercises.prompt: Listen to the three phrases (four notes each). Which form did you hear?
exercises.hint: Call the first phrase A. Is each next phrase the same or new?
exercises.explain: A new phrase came second, then it came again: A B B.

exercises.prompt: A bridge usually comes many times in a song.
exercises.hint: Why is it called a bridge?
exercises.explain: False: a bridge usually comes once, near the end, to lead to the last chorus.

exercises.prompt: Listen to the three phrases (four notes each). Which form did you hear?
exercises.hint: Call the first phrase A. Is each next phrase the same or new?
exercises.explain: The first phrase came back after a new one: A B A.
A keeps coming back between B and C: rondo form.

exercises.prompt: A rondo goes A B A C A D A. How many times is A played?
exercises.explain: A B A C A D A: A comes 4 times.

exercises.prompt: Listen to the three phrases (four notes each). Which form did you hear?
exercises.hint: Are any phrases the same as an earlier one?
exercises.explain: All three phrases are different: A B C.

exercises.prompt: Why does a bridge make the last chorus feel fresh?
exercises.hint: What happens when you hear something new before something you know?
choices: It is different, so the chorus sounds new again
exercises.explain: The bridge brings something different, so when the chorus comes back it feels fresh.

exercises.prompt: Listen to the three phrases (four notes each). Which form did you hear?
exercises.hint: Is the second phrase the same as the first?
exercises.explain: The first phrase came twice, then a new one: A A B.

exercises.prompt: In a song, which stay the same every time, and which change?
exercises.hint: Verses tell more of the story each time.
exercises.explain: The chorus's words and tune and the verse's tune stay the same. The verse's words change.

exercises.prompt: Each verse lasts 16 bars and each chorus 8 bars. A song has 2 verses and 3 choruses. How many bars is that?
exercises.hint: Work out the verses and the choruses, then add them.
exercises.explain: Verses: 2 × 16 = 32 bars. Choruses: 3 × 8 = 24 bars. In all: 32 + 24 = 56 bars.
